area.title: Address book: add and edit an address
area.scope: Adding an address to the address book (choosing a type or category, manual entry, the fields, roles and their hints, validation, saving, the return to a journey section or contact address, and the add handshake on the INS side) and editing an address (prefill, fields, validation, save and cancel); the address record, its fields and validation, and the create, read-one, update and delete APIs and their error shapes. Stops at the list, view and delete pages (address-book-list) and at finding an address by postcode (address-lookup).

sources.role: the answers to the two notification view header questions the 25 November re-distil raised from ruling:sam-2026-11-19 point 2. It settles c-438: once the amend confirmation page exists, 'Amend this notification' on the header is a link to that page rather than a posting button, because the first click then changes nothing, a POST that only renders a page is the wrong verb and leaves a re-POST on the back button without JavaScript, and Delete already opens its confirmation page by href in the same header; Copy as new keeps its own form because it still changes something, Delete stays a link, and no action shares another's form, in live animals, germinal products and plants alike. Point 2 of the 19 November ruling is unweakened, its subject being that no action shares another action's form, which a link does not do. It settles c-447 the other way from the default: the plants header gains a Copy as new action so both journeys offer the same three actions. That is wiring rather than a feature build, because every layer beneath it is already on main - the plants backend serves POST /{referenceNumber}/copy with a NotificationCopyMapper, the plants frontend's real and stub persistence both implement copy, and its engine holds copyJourney - and only the header's copyAction and route are missing. The plants backend therefore needs nothing and trade-imports-plants-backend does not join this programme's repos; inc-123 takes plantsfrontend alongside backend, frontend and tests, and inc-124's stale-copy return takes plants too. Plants' copy carries plants' own answers, so the carried-over-trade against cleared-shipment split is read against plants' own fields rather than copied field for field.

sources.role: the decision that pagination is kept everywhere and that its earlier removal was an error: every address book list and every address picker pages, and no requirement says a list of an organisation's addresses is served or shown unpaginated. It drops req-611's 'unpaginated' clause and supersedes ruling:ian-2026-11-23 point 6 on that point alone, because that point's reasoning rested on the address book's list endpoint taking no role and so having to be read whole and paged for display, which is no longer true of the service: RequestedListFilters takes roles and searchRoles, AddressController lists one page at a time with page and pageSize, and ListPaging sets 1 to 100 defaulting to 25, exactly the bounds ruling:paul-2026-11-05 point 8 names. The role filter runs in the service before the page is cut, so paging the API cannot make it wrong, and Paul's point 8 stands in full. The rest of ruling:ian-2026-11-23 stands: the pickers page at eight, the one-page clause of inc-087's criteria 7, 8 and 9 stays dropped with req-594 and req-595, and the 'Selected address' restatement comes back with the paging. EUDPA-827 is the fix and has landed on the animals frontend's main. It settles conflict c-292 by keeping the plants contact picker's pagination and inset, and the contact picker pages at eight rather than five, confirmed by Ian the same day, so every picker in both journeys pages at the figure the INS address book list already uses and ruling:ian-2026-11-23 point 1 set for the other pickers.

sources.role: the decision on transporter management, outranking ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm on that point and lifting claim c-285: the address book manages transporters as per-organisation records, and adding one mid journey uses the address book hand-off already built for addresses (inc-077, inc-078, inc-080). A transporter is its own record in its own transporters collection inside the address book service, not the Address model; it has no roles and stores a private-or-commercial type instead; a commercial transporter country is forced to XI (Northern Ireland) with no reference-data lookup, while a private transporter keeps its choice of export country. Approved transporters are parked.

claims.statement: This ruling settles whether the service manages transporters at all and, if so, whether the address book or something else does - the question ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm point 5 (claim c-285) left blocked pending requirements.
claims.quote: On transporter management, which Sam's ruling of 9 October (afternoon) left blocked pending requirements — whether the service manages transporters at all and, if so, whether the address book or something else does (`ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm` point 5, claim c-285):
claims.note: answers the block ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm point 5 left, recorded there as claim c-285

claims.statement: The address book manages transporters, which are saved per organisation just like other addresses.
claims.quote: My decision is that the address book will manage the transporters, just like other addresses which are saved per organisation.

claims.statement: Adding a transporter uses the same pattern of moving to the address book mid journey that adding other addresses uses.
claims.quote: It will use the same pattern with moving to the address book mid journey, like other addresses when adding transporters - it's essentially the same pattern.

claims.statement: The earlier block rested on the concept of 'approved transporters': a list that may be managed in MDM for all organisations and added to each organisation's own transporter options.
claims.quote: I think that previous ruling was based on the concept of 'approved transporters' which may be a list managed in MDM for all organisations that will be added to the organisations individual transporter options.

claims.statement: Approved transporters are not to be worried about for now.

sources.role: the decision on what the address book stores for an address's type and uses (EUDPA-711): "use" is renamed "role" everywhere, in the record, the API, the code, the copy keys, the tests and the spec, and an address holds the roles it can play on a notification, being place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer, place of destination and branch address. The address book stores roles only and requires at least one; it does not store an address type and ignores one a client sends, the address type being the INS front door's grouping of roles worked out from them. The grouping of roles into sending, receiving and branch is the address book's internal rule rather than part of its API, and it refuses roles from more than one group, and a consignee, importer or place of destination outside the United Kingdom. The list takes role, repeatable and any-of, and searchRole, in place of addressType, use and searchUse. A role a new notification type needs is added in code, each role in exactly one group. Addresses saved before the change are not migrated: after release the addresses collection is dropped in dev and test with CDP tooling and the address book restarted, and locally the stack is restarted. The address book's list and every address picker keep pagination even though the Design Release 2.1 prototype has none, the list API paging with page and pageSize of 1 to 100 defaulting to 25, because organisations in test environments hold thousands of addresses; no requirement to list an organisation's addresses unpaginated is built, which ruling:ian-2026-11-23 point 6 later reads the other way for req-611 and so outranks on that point alone.

sources.role: the owner's decisions: outranks every other source. Search boxes use the real frontend's accessible component with MDM's entries. JavaScript behaviour follows the toolbox rule with graceful degradation; JavaScript-only prototype behaviour, pop-ups included, waits on design in its own theme. Commodity catalogue and search wait on MDM; transporter management waits on requirements; the INS dashboard's summary information waits on its requirements. The overview, review, declaration and confirmation are set-owned, and shared parts change add-only. Where plants has the same page or behaviour, the same increment changes it. Each notification list is reframed in its own frontend. The report groups work as ready or blocked. Claims marked as the orchestrator's apply Sam's principles and are not his rulings; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-templates covers templates and the dashboard narrowing.

claims.statement: Sam rules that, as a pre-step for these increments, three questions are answered: is it possible with off-the-shelf GDS; if not, with other complementary off-the-shelf components; if not, why is the atypical thing strongly required. The ruling does not say which override wins when a DR1 judgement and a real constraint the prototype cannot express point different ways on the same difference.
The ruling does not say what a real service does where a real constraint overrides the prototype: whether it keeps today's behaviour or matches the prototype as closely as the constraint allows.
The ruling does not say whether a feature or behaviour a real service has that Design Release 2.1 does not show at all counts as a difference to remove, or is left alone.
The ruling does not say what to do where the code two themes need to touch overlaps, so no boundary keeps their pull requests from conflicting.

sources.role: what exists today and what has already been ruled; the real persistence, validation and authorisation constraints the prototype cannot express

claims.statement: An address is stored as a document in the MongoDB collection named addresses, owned by one organisation.
claims.quote:
/** An organisation-owned address-book entry. {@code roles} can be null or empty. */
@Document(collection = "addresses")

claims.statement: The stored address holds these fields: id, name, addressLine1, addressLine2, townOrCity, county, postcode, countryCode, phone, email (all strings), roles (a list of address roles), organisationId (string), status (ACTIVE or DELETED), createdAt, modifiedAt and expireAt (instants), and version (a number).
claims.note: The stored record has no address type field: roles replaced it.

claims.statement: A stored address's roles may be null or empty: the record itself does not require a role, only the request does.
claims.quote: {@code roles} can be null or empty.

claims.statement: The address's createdAt is set by the database auditing when it is first saved, and modifiedAt each time it is saved.
A stored address carries a version number, which inferred from the Spring Data @Version annotation gives optimistic locking: a save against a stale version is refused.
claims.quote:
@Version
  private Long version;
claims.note: mechanism: version counter on the stored address. How a conflict answers over HTTP is part 2's.

claims.statement: Addresses are indexed by organisation, then status, then newest created first (index org_status_created).
Two addresses are the same address when their ids are equal, whatever their other fields hold.
claims.note: mechanism: identity of the stored address.

claims.statement: An address's status is ACTIVE or DELETED; DELETED is a soft-delete tombstone that is left out of lists but can still be read by id.
claims.quote:
Soft-delete tombstone status. {@code DELETED} addresses are excluded from lists but remain
 * readable by id. The enum is never on the wire.

claims.statement: The status value is never sent on the wire; a read shows a deleted boolean instead.
claims.quote: Soft-deleted addresses expose `deleted: true` on read; the internal `status` enum is not on the wire.

claims.statement: The create and replace request body has the fields name, addressLine1, addressLine2, townOrCity, county, postcode, countryCode, phone, email and roles, all camelCase under their Java names.
claims.quote: Create/update request body. Every field is camelCase on the wire, under its Java name.

claims.statement: A request body that echoes server-assigned fields (id, organisationId, deleted, status, createdAt, modifiedAt) is accepted, and those values are dropped rather than saved.
claims.quote:
Server-assigned fields ({@code id}, {@code organisationId}, {@code deleted}, timestamps) are
 * not components, so a body that echoes them is accepted and they are dropped.
claims.note: The test request_deserialisesFromCamelCaseAndMapsOntoAnEntityIgnoringServerFields sends id, organisationId 'OTHER-ORG', status 'DELETED', deleted true and both timestamps and proves each is null on the entity.

claims.statement: roles is required on create and on update: a missing or empty roles list is refused with 'Select what this address can be used for'.
claims.quote: @NotEmpty(message = "Select what this address can be used for")

claims.statement: A missing roles list is read as an empty list, so it fails the required-roles rule rather than erroring.
claims.quote:
{@code roles} is never null: a missing list reads as empty, and repeated roles collapse to
 * their first occurrence.

claims.statement: A role repeated in the request collapses to its first occurrence, keeping the order the caller sent: CONSIGNOR, PLACE_OF_ORIGIN, CONSIGNOR becomes CONSIGNOR, PLACE_OF_ORIGIN.
claims.quote: roles = roles == null ? List.of() : roles.stream().distinct().toList();

claims.statement: Every role in the request must be one of the five role names exactly; an unknown name (such as TRANSPORTER), a lower-case name (such as consignor), a null entry or a blank entry is refused with 'Select valid roles', keyed by roles.
claims.quote: @AddressRoleNames(message = "Select valid roles")

claims.statement: An unknown role name is reported as a field error on roles beside the other field errors, rather than failing the whole body before validation, so every other field error is still shown.
claims.quote: An unknown enum constant would make Jackson throw before validation, which answers as a `bad-request` problem with no `errors` map and hides every other field error. A string component fails Bean Validation, so the `validation-error` problem names `roles` beside the other field errors.
claims.note: mechanism: roles carried as strings in the request and checked by name. The error key is roles, never roles[1].

claims.statement: A request whose only role is unknown gets exactly one violation, on roles: the one-group rule ignores names that are not roles.
claims.quote: It skips role names that are not roles; `@AddressRoleNames` reports those.

claims.statement: There are five address roles: PLACE_OF_ORIGIN, CONSIGNOR, PLACE_OF_DESTINATION, CONSIGNEE and IMPORTER, each a party or a place a notification can choose the address for.
claims.quote: /** A role a notification can choose this address for: a party, or a place. */

claims.statement: The API describes each role: PLACE_OF_ORIGIN 'Where the animals or goods start their journey', CONSIGNOR 'The party sending the consignment', PLACE_OF_DESTINATION 'Where the animals or goods are unloaded in Great Britain', CONSIGNEE 'The party receiving the consignment', IMPORTER 'The party importing the consignment'.
claims.note: The address book holds no display labels for roles; labels are the caller's copy (README Design notes).

claims.statement: Each role belongs to one of two groups: sending (PLACE_OF_ORIGIN, CONSIGNOR) or receiving (CONSIGNEE, IMPORTER, PLACE_OF_DESTINATION).
claims.quote:
| Sending | `PLACE_OF_ORIGIN`, `CONSIGNOR` |
| Receiving | `CONSIGNEE`, `IMPORTER`, `PLACE_OF_DESTINATION` |

claims.statement: The role groups are internal: they are not part of the API, and a caller only sees them as a refusal. A new role cannot be added without a group.
claims.quote:
Each `AddressRole` names its one group (`RoleGroup`), so a new
role cannot be added without a group. The grouping is internal: it is not part of the API, and a
caller only sees it as a refusal.

claims.statement: An address's roles must all come from one group; a request mixing sending and receiving roles (such as PLACE_OF_ORIGIN with CONSIGNEE) is refused with 'An address can only have roles from one group', keyed by roles, on both create and update.
claims.quote: String message() default "An address can only have roles from one group";
claims.note: README: 'The rule belongs to the address book.' The class-level violation is attached to the roles property so it sits beside the field errors.

claims.statement: An address may hold every role of one group together: PLACE_OF_ORIGIN with CONSIGNOR, or CONSIGNEE with IMPORTER and PLACE_OF_DESTINATION, is accepted.

claims.quote: @BeanMapping(ignoreUnmappedSourceProperties = {"status", "version", "expireAt"})

claims.quote: a cross-organisation request and an unknown id are deliberately indistinguishable, so the address book never confirms that another organisation holds a given id.

claims.statement: A 404 is never a deletion signal: only a 200 with deleted: true means the address was deleted.

claims.quote: Outside prod it can also mean the address has expired (see below).

claims.statement: An address is replaced with PUT /organisation/{orgId}/addresses/{address-id}, taking a full AddressRequest body, and a success answers 200 with the updated address.
claims.quote: operationId: update-address summary: Replace an address's mutable fields ... '200': description: Updated address with bumped modifiedAt

claims.statement: modifiedAt is an audit timestamp only: it is not used as a precondition on a replace.
claims.quote: {@code modifiedAt} is bumped on success (audit only).

claims.statement: A replace of a soft-deleted address (a tombstone) answers 404 with the not-found problem and no errors map, and changes nothing.
claims.quote: An unknown id, an id outside the caller's organisation, or a soft-deleted tombstone all yield a 404 — tombstones are outside the caller's live set and existence is never leaked.

claims.statement: A replace of an unknown address id, or of another organisation's address id, answers 404 with the not-found problem.
claims.quote: .andExpect(status().isNotFound()) .andExpect(jsonPath("$.type").value("https://api.cdp.defra.cloud/problems/not-found"));

claims.statement: A create or replace with an invalid body answers 400 with the validation-error problem, its errors map naming each rejected field, and saves nothing: a refused create stores no address and a refused replace leaves the stored address untouched.

claims.statement: A replace whose address was changed by another request since it was read answers 409 with the conflict problem.

claims.statement: Every address save is version-checked: a save from a copy read before a later replace is refused rather than overwriting it.
claims.quote: assertThatThrownBy(() -> addressRepository.save(stale)) .isInstanceOf(OptimisticLockingFailureException.class);
claims.note: mechanism: optimistic locking on the stored address document.

claims.statement: The address book logs each replace with the address id and the organisation id.

claims.statement: An address is soft-deleted with DELETE /organisation/{orgId}/addresses/{address-id}, which answers 204 No Content with no body.
claims.quote: operationId: delete-address summary: Soft-delete an address (tombstone) ... '204': description: Soft-deleted (or already deleted — idempotent)

claims.statement: A delete keeps the address: its status flips to DELETED, modifiedAt moves later and createdAt is unchanged.
claims.quote: The document is not removed: {@code status} flips to {@code DELETED} and {@code modifiedAt} is bumped, and the tombstone stays fetchable by id so a deletion is detectable.

claims.statement: After a delete the address drops out of the list (totalItems 0, no items) but GET by its id still answers 200 with deleted: true.
claims.quote: Tombstones are excluded from list results.

claims.statement: Deleting an already-deleted address is idempotent: it answers 204 and changes nothing, not even modifiedAt.
claims.quote: Idempotent — deleting an already-DELETED address is a 204 with no state change.

claims.statement: A delete of an unknown address id answers 404 with the not-found problem.
claims.quote: .andExpect(status().isNotFound()) .andExpect(header().string("Content-Type", MediaType.APPLICATION_PROBLEM_JSON_VALUE)) .andExpect(jsonPath("$.type").value("https://api.cdp.defra.cloud/problems/not-found")) .andExpect(jsonPath("$.status").value(404));

claims.statement: A delete of another organisation's address answers 404 and leaves that address active, whether the caller uses its own organisation in the path or a path organisation that disagrees with its header.
claims.quote: deleteAddressAs(OTHER_ORG, OTHER_ORG, saved.getId()) .andExpect(status().isNotFound()); ... .isEqualTo(AddressStatus.ACTIVE);

claims.statement: A deleted address cannot be brought back by a stale write: a save from a copy read before the delete is refused and the address stays DELETED.
claims.quote: stale.setStatus(AddressStatus.ACTIVE); assertThatThrownBy(() -> repository.save(stale)) .isInstanceOf(OptimisticLockingFailureException.class);
claims.note: mechanism: optimistic locking on the stored address document.

claims.statement: The address book logs a soft delete with the address id and the organisation id, and logs a repeat delete as already deleted and left unchanged.

claims.statement: Soft delete exists so a consumer can tell a deleted address from an unknown one: a hard delete would make both answer 404.
claims.quote: Why soft delete: a hard delete would make a deleted address look the same as an unknown one (both 404), so a consumer could never tell that an address had been deleted.

claims.statement: In prod, addresses and their tombstones are kept indefinitely.
claims.quote: In prod, addresses, transporters and their tombstones are retained indefinitely (~1 KB each).

claims.statement: Every single-address operation requires the Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id header and the orgId and (except create) address-id path parameters; a missing header is a 400 problem, and a path orgId that disagrees with the header is a 404 on create.
claims.quote: '400': description: Validation error, or a missing identity header ... '404': description: Path orgId does not match the caller's organisation header ... '400': description: Missing org header
claims.note: How the header is checked and the scoping rule itself belong to part 3; this claim records only the statuses these four operations declare.

claims.statement: The GET operation declares no 400 response, unlike create, replace and delete, which each declare one for a missing header.
claims.quote: responses: '200': description: The address (deleted false or true) ... '404': ... '500':
claims.note: Inferred from the absence of a 400 entry on get-address in both the controller annotations and the generated OpenAPI; the header is still required. Whether a missing header on GET answers 400 is for part 3 to say.

claims.statement: Every single-address operation declares a 500 response with the problem body, and the 404 responses of get, replace and delete name an unknown id or an id outside the caller's organisation (and, for replace, a tombstone).
claims.quote: '404': description: Unknown id, an id outside the caller's organisation scope, or a tombstone ... '500': description: Unexpected server error

claims.statement: Every error response is RFC 9457 problem details with Content-Type application/problem+json.
claims.quote: Global exception handler producing RFC 9457 {@code application/problem+json} responses, CDP problem-family type URIs and a camelCase {@code traceId} extension.

claims.statement: A problem body has type, title and status (required), and optionally detail and traceId; a field left empty is omitted from the body.
claims.quote: @JsonInclude(JsonInclude.Include.NON_NULL) ... public record Problem( @Schema(requiredMode = Schema.RequiredMode.REQUIRED) String type, @Schema(requiredMode = Schema.RequiredMode.REQUIRED) String title, @Schema(requiredMode = Schema.RequiredMode.REQUIRED) Integer status, String detail, String traceId) {}

claims.statement: A validation problem body has the same fields as a problem plus a required errors map from each field name to a list of messages.
claims.quote: RFC 9457 validation problem body with a per-field camelCase {@code errors} map. ... errors: type: object additionalProperties: type: array items: type: string required: - errors

claims.statement: No problem body carries instance, so a cross-organisation 404 is identical to an unknown-id 404.
claims.quote: Responses use the service's own `Problem` and `ValidationProblem` records rather than Spring's `ProblemDetail`, so no body carries `instance`. A request-scoped URI would carry path ids and let a cross-organisation 404 differ from an unknown-id 404.

claims.statement: A problem body carries the request's trace id as traceId when one is set, and leaves traceId out when none is.
claims.quote: private static final String MDC_TRACE_ID = "trace.id"; ... assertThat(response.getBody().traceId()).isNull();

claims.statement: A field-validation failure answers 400 with type https://api.cdp.defra.cloud/problems/validation-error, title "Validation Error" and detail "Validation failed for one or more fields".
claims.quote: PROBLEM_BASE + "validation-error", "Validation Error", HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST.value(), "Validation failed for one or more fields",

claims.statement: The validation problem's errors map is keyed by the rejected field's camelCase name, such as addressLine1, never a snake_case name such as address_line_1.
claims.quote: .andExpect(jsonPath("$.errors.addressLine1").exists()) .andExpect(jsonPath("$.errors.email").exists()) .andExpect(jsonPath("$.errors.address_line_1").doesNotExist());

claims.statement: When one field fails several checks, all its messages are listed under that one field in the errors map, in the order raised.
claims.quote: assertThat(response.getBody().errors().get("name")) .containsExactly("must not be blank", "size must be at most 255");

claims.statement: Every 400 other than a field-validation failure is the bad-request problem: type https://api.cdp.defra.cloud/problems/bad-request, title "Bad Request", status 400, and no errors key.
claims.quote: A field-validation failure ({@link MethodArgumentNotValidException}) carries an {@code errors} map keyed by the rejected field's Java name, such as {@code addressLine1}. Every other 400 carries no {@code errors} key.

claims.statement: A malformed JSON body on create, or an empty body on replace, answers 400 with the bad-request problem, detail "Malformed JSON request body", and saves nothing.
claims.quote: "Malformed JSON request body",

claims.statement: A query or path parameter that cannot be read as its type answers 400 with the bad-request problem and detail "Invalid value for parameter '<name>'" naming the parameter.
claims.quote: "Invalid value for parameter '" + ex.getName() + "'",

claims.statement: A service-level bad request answers 400 with the bad-request problem whose detail is the refusal's own message.
claims.quote: problem(HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST, "bad-request", "Bad Request", ex.getMessage(), traceId));

claims.statement: The validation-error and bad-request problems are two distinct 400 shapes: both status 400, different types, and only the validation one has an errors map.
claims.quote: assertThat(validation.status()).isEqualTo(badRequest.status()); assertThat(validation.errors()).isNotEmpty(); assertThat(badRequest.type()).isNotEqualTo(validation.type());

claims.statement: Create and replace declare their 400 as anyOf the validation problem or the plain problem, not oneOf.
claims.quote: POST and PUT declare their 400 as `anyOf(ValidationProblem, Problem)`, not `oneOf`: a field-validation failure carries an `errors` map and every other 400 carries none.

claims.statement: A not-found answers 404 with type https://api.cdp.defra.cloud/problems/not-found, title "Resource Not Found" and, for an address, detail "Address not found".
claims.quote: problem( HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, "not-found", "Resource Not Found", ex.detail(), traceId)); ... return new NotFoundException( "Address not found",

claims.quote: The caller sees only {@link #detail()}; the message names the case and its ids. ... "Organisation mismatch: path orgId " + orgId + " is not the caller's organisation " + organisationId

claims.statement: A concurrent update conflict answers 409 with type https://api.cdp.defra.cloud/problems/conflict, title "Conflict" and detail "The resource was modified by another request".
claims.quote: HttpStatus.CONFLICT, "conflict", "Conflict", "The resource was modified by another request",

claims.statement: An unexpected error answers 500 with type https://api.cdp.defra.cloud/problems/internal-error, title "Internal Server Error" and detail "An unexpected error occurred. Please try again later.", and is logged at error with the exception.
claims.quote: "internal-error", "Internal Server Error", "An unexpected error occurred. Please try again later.",

claims.statement: A validation failure is logged at warn with the trace id and the rejected field names only, never the rejected values or the exception, because the values can be personal data.
claims.quote: A validation failure is logged with the rejected field names only. The exception's message holds the rejected values, which can be personal data, so it is not logged.

claims.statement: Every other refusal (malformed parameter, malformed body, bad request, not found, conflict) is logged at warn with the trace id, the reason and the exception.
claims.quote: log.warn("Malformed parameter (trace: {}): {}", traceId, ex.getMessage(), ex); ... log.warn("Optimistic locking failure (trace: {}): {}", traceId, ex.getMessage(), ex);

claims.statement: The controller logs each single-address request at info with the address id only (or, for create, no id), never the request body.
claims.quote: log.info("POST addresses - creating address"); ... log.info("GET addresses/{}", addressId); ... log.info("PUT addresses/{}", addressId); ... log.info("DELETE addresses/{}", addressId);

claims.statement: The README's route table lists the four single-address operations: POST to create, GET one address (tombstones included), PUT a full replace of mutable fields, and DELETE a soft delete answering an idempotent 204.

claims.statement: JSON properties on the wire are camelCase, and validation failures return 400 application/problem+json with a camelCase errors map.
claims.quote: JSON properties are **camelCase** (e.g. `addressLine1`, `countryCode`, `pageSize`). ... Validation failures return **400** `application/problem+json` with a camelCase `errors` map.

claims.statement: An addressType in a create body is ignored: the create answers 201, the response and later reads carry no addressType, and the roles sent are kept.
claims.quote: An `addressType` in a body is ignored.
claims.note: Sits on the edge of part 1's field rules; claimed here as create-path behaviour.

claims.statement: No replace test proves that a body's echoed read-only fields (id, organisationId, deleted, createdAt) are ignored on PUT, as AddressCrudIT proves for POST.
claims.note: AddressServiceTest proves the service keeps id, organisationId, status and createdAt on replace from a request that cannot carry them; no IT sends them in a PUT body.

claims.statement: The API describes the request body as 'Create or replace an address in the caller's address book'.
claims.quote: @Schema(description = "Create or replace an address in the caller's address book")

claims.statement: The API describes addressLine2 in the request as 'Second line of the postal address'.
claims.quote: @Schema(description = "Second line of the postal address", maxLength = 255)

claims.statement: The API describes the response as 'An address in the caller's organisation-scoped address book', and its name field as 'Display name'.

The code and the generated API document disagree on whether a response's roles is required: AddressResponse marks roles as required (and always sends a list, empty when none), but docs/openapi/addresses.yml leaves roles out of the AddressResponse required list.
claims.quote:
arraySchema =
                @Schema(
                    description =
                        "The roles a notification can choose this address for; empty when it has"
                            + " none",
                    requiredMode = Schema.RequiredMode.REQUIRED))
        List<AddressRole> roles,
claims.note: Inferred from comparing the annotation with the yml: springdoc appears not to carry requiredMode from an @ArraySchema's arraySchema into the required list. In practice the field is always present because the compact constructor turns null into an empty list.

claims.statement: Over HTTP, a path orgId that differs from the organisation header is refused by the header filter before any controller runs. Its 404 detail is "Resource not found", so it differs from an unknown-address 404, whose detail is "Address not found". The equal bodies that GlobalExceptionHandlerTest proves apply only to the controller's own organisation check, which the filter reaches first.
claims.quote: NotFoundException.organisationMismatch(pathOrgId, organisationId, "Resource not found");
claims.note: Inferred from the filter running at HIGHEST_PRECEDENCE + 1 on every /organisation/ path before the controller's OrganisationScope.authorise call. The detail differs, and type, title and status are the same. Reconcile should decide whether the two 404 details should match, given the README's 'no existence disclosure' aim.

claims.statement: The address-book API creates a record for an organisation with POST /organisation/{organisationId}/addresses and a JSON body of name, addressLine1, townOrCity, postcode, countryCode, phone and email, answering 201 with a Location header for the new record.
claims.quote: {"name":"Danish Meat Export Kolding1791394803707","addressLine1":"Havnegade 21","townOrCity":"Copenhagen","postcode":"1058","countryCode":"DK","phone":"01228 555 0197","email":"searchable@example.co.uk"} -> 201 Location: http://localhost:8089/organisation/5900001/addresses/6ac683f36bdb2fc53f12860e
claims.note: Called by the test to seed records, not by a page; it shows the system of record behind the picker.

claims.statement: An address-book record carries id, name, addressLine1, addressLine2, townOrCity, county, postcode, countryCode, phone, email, organisationId, a deleted flag, createdAt and modifiedAt.

claims.statement: The address book add handshake takes four query parameters on /address-book/add: journey-type, notification-id, fulfilment-id and handshake-token.
claims.quote: /address-book/add?journey-type=not-a-journey&notification-id=GBN-AG-26-4F7K2P&fulfilment-id=9ad1e2f3-a4b5-4c60-8d1c-9e0f1a2b3c4d&handshake-token=handshake-token-value
claims.note: The handshake-token value in the trace is a test placeholder, not a credential.

claims.statement: An add handshake whose journey-type is not a recognised journey is refused with HTTP 404, by a signed-in user.
claims.quote: GET 404 http://localhost:3002/address-book/add?journey-type=not-a-journey

claims.statement: The refusal renders the INS 404 page: heading 404, body Page not found, title Page not found | Import notification service, with the Address book navigation item active and no back link or onward link in the page body.
claims.quote: 404 Page not found

claims.statement: No trace shows the add handshake with a recognised journey type: what the add page shows when a journey hands off to it, and how it returns the new address to the journey, are not evidenced.
The add page is headed Add address details and has no back link.
claims.quote: Add address details
claims.note: No back link appears above main on the add page, while the edit and delete pages have one.

claims.statement: Saving the add form posts every field, with a CSRF crumb, to /address-book/add and redirects (302) to /address-book.

claims.statement: A created address persists with its full Standard Address Block: the record written to the address book store holds the address line 2 and county the user entered.
claims.quote: expect(doc.addressLine2).toBe(details.addressLine2); expect(doc.county).toBe(details.county);
claims.note: Store is the trade-imports-address-book database, addresses collection. The browser trace cannot show Mongo; the assertion held because the test passed.
